subject: Detecting files with errors in part5

messages.author: c2b608cf1a4e77a3
messages.subject: Detecting files with errors in part5
parts:
Hi Vincent, Jairo and colleagues,

While processing accelerometer data in version 2.0 in the past, I remember that GGIR skipped files that could not be processed. Now I am currently processing 2.000 gt3x+ CSV files in GGIR 2.8-2 and GGIR has stopped several times when a specific function could not be applied. When the errors occurred in part1 or part2, the output provided the file name, so I was able to inspect the file. In part5, however,  I have no information about which file has errors to exclude before running GGIR again. So, I have the following questions:

1. Is there a way to make GGIR skipp files with errors and continue processing the remaining data?

2. Is there an argument that provides more detailed part5 output while the data is being processed (e.g., mentioning the file name such as print.filename in part1)?

To illustrate, the error I get when GGIR stops at part5 is below. Probably this file has issue with valid nights, but I was not able to locate the file to inspect.
 Error in if (nightsi[1] == 1) wi = wi + 1 :  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Thank you for your support,
Regards,
Marcus Lopes

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Detecting files with errors in part5
parts:
Hi Marcus,

1. Are you using "do.parallel = TRUE"? This is default option in GGIR. I think the processing will continue even if some of the files provide error messages when using "do.parallel = TRUE".

2. To facilitate debugging errors, I would suggest to run once GGIR with "do.parallel = FALSE" and "overwrite = FALSE", so that you can see what is the file index that provided the error (then you can check what this file is in the e.g. "meta/ms3.out" folder (the file index indicates the position of the file in alphabetical order).

Hope this helps.

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: c2b608cf1a4e77a3
messages.subject: Re: Detecting files with errors in part5
parts:
Hi Jairo,

1. I included the Verisense step algorithm as an additional function. The function documentation recommended to avoid using the "do.parallel=TRUE" argument. So I processed part1 and part2 with  "do.parallel=FALSE" and now I am processing part3-5 with  "do.parallel=TRUE". The processing is not being paused due to errors, thank you for the suggestion.

2. The alphabetical order of files within the "meta/ms3.out" is different from the processing order (e.g., the file 9 is followed by file 10 in windows, but by file 91 in GGIR). Apparently, the GGIR requires zeros at the left to order as Windows. I will look for an alternative for ordering the same way in windows.

Thank you for your support.

Best,
Marcus.
